content:
According to the Financial Times, newly revealed court documents show that OpenAI is disappointed with the adoption of ChatGPT through Apple Intelligence, claiming the integration "performed far below expectations" since its launch in 2024. Here's the full story.

OpenAI Asks Court to Rule Before Trial

In August 2025, Elon Musk said X, now merged into SpaceXAI, would sue Apple and OpenAI over alleged collusion to shut out AI competitors, stemming from OpenAI's deal to integrate ChatGPT into Apple Intelligence and Siri.

When the suit was formally filed, the scope of the complaints actually went beyond the App Store ranking issues Musk originally publicly criticised. X and SpaceXAI also accused Apple of trying to strangle the development of "super apps," including X's own efforts to turn itself into an "everything app".

In the weeks and months that followed, all the companies involved filed briefs, accusations and rebuttals with the court. Apple and OpenAI have consistently argued the deal is not the exclusive partnership the complaint alleges, while the court filings have also revealed new details about the collaboration between the two.

One such detail was exposed in a filing OpenAI made today. As the Financial Times first reported, OpenAI "said it was disappointed by how little interest Apple generated among iPhone users after the 2024 deal to power 'Apple Intelligence' with ChatGPT".

The report continues:

Wednesday's court filings stated that when the 2024 deal was struck, OpenAI expected to see a "halo effect" from Apple's promotion and brand association, and anticipated more subscriptions from Apple Intelligence users. But one month after the ChatGPT integration launched, the "start was visibly slow," and OpenAI revised down its projections for weekly active users it could attract. By summer 2025, "it had become clear that Apple's integration of ChatGPT had performed far below expectations."

The report notes that today's filing contains multiple redacted exchanges, but the unredacted portions show OpenAI executives worrying Apple might "want to move faster" to find another AI partner.

When Apple Intelligence was first unveiled in 2024, Craig Federighi said in an interview that Apple ultimately wanted users to be able to choose between different AI models, specifically naming Google Gemini as a potential future integration option.

That particular partnership never came together, but Apple has since turned to Google's Gemini model to help power the new Siri AI, while Xcode has also expanded to support coding agents from Anthropic, Google and OpenAI.

The top-liked comment was posted by OliveCocktail

As others have said, when I want ChatGPT, I go straight to its standalone app. In fact, that's my preference, because I don't want all my voice requests mixed together. I'd rather Apple handle my personal and contextually relevant stuff. I've never been clear on the privacy implications of using the ChatGPT "integration," and I haven't even wanted to find out, because I know I won't use it. By contrast, with Apple Intelligence/Siri, I feel comfortable about the privacy side and can use it with peace of mind.

Returning to today's filings, the Financial Times notes the documents also suggest that the way Apple implemented ChatGPT may be one of the reasons for the slow uptake, as the integration is off by default.

Finally, according to Reuters, OpenAI is also arguing that SpaceX's recent securities disclosures are sufficient to undermine SpaceXAI's claims that the Apple deal harms competition. In the filing, OpenAI said SpaceX's registration statement for its public listing is full of disclosures that are "directly contrary to the competitive harm alleged in the lawsuit".

On these grounds, OpenAI is asking Judge Mark Pittman to rule in its favour on SpaceXAI's antitrust claims before trial. The case is currently scheduled to go to trial in January.
